headline: Lazard is bullish on Eagers Automotive citing structural cost advantages and surging BYD sales driving potential earnings upgrades
reasoning: Binsted highlights that Eagers reported Australian business tracking 5% ahead of prior comparable period at its AGM in May, while competitors Peter Warren and ASG Group are reporting near-zero profits and significant earnings downgrades respectively. He attributes Eagers' outperformance to a structurally more efficient cost base. More importantly, BYD June car sales in Australia surged to over 18,000 units (approximately 18% market share) versus a prior run-rate of 7,000-8,000 units (6-7% market share), suggesting underlying demand may be 9-11% market share. Eagers holds approximately 80% of BYD's retail joint venture in Australia and commands around 30% market share of new energy vehicles versus 11% of total new car sales, positioning the company to benefit significantly from EV adoption. This BYD data could drive consensus earnings upgrades.
quote: So a couple of really interesting things. First of all, they came with an update at the AGM in May, and they said that the Australian business was tracking about 5% ahead of PCP, which is strong, bit less than market expectations, but strong. Shortly after we saw Peter Warren come out and say basically they are making zero profit this half. Very tough industry conditions and ASG Group, their other big listed competitor, big earnings downgrade. So IG is still showing growth while their main competitors are almost making no money. What are they doing right. That they're the others aren't. Look two things. So cost base. They have a much more efficient cost base structural cost advantage. But the big one, and this is the sort of news that I think makes Edgars topical right now, is just in early July this week we have the figures for June car sales. BYD sold more than 18,000 cars in June. Now this is this is huge. Before this, they were tracking at about 7 to 8000 units a month, which is, you know, relative to our car market, call it 6 to 7% market share. That June number is something like 18% market share. Now, that's not all just in one month, but it shows that in the preceding months they were selling a lot more cars than they were delivering. So the underlying demand could be nine, ten, 11% market share, which if that rolls through, which seems likely given it's a sustained order right above deliveries, that could mean upgrades for figures relative to consensus.
episode_title: Why Eagers Automotive is in the driver's seat

headline: Lazard's Aaron Binsted sees potential turnaround in Treasury Wine Estates following investor day guidance that signals earnings stability at the bottom of a two-year decline.
reasoning: After two years of pain for shareholders driven by China's alcohol ban at events and US overstock issues, new CEO Sam Fisher provided FY26 earnings guidance slightly above market expectations at a May investor day, and indicated FY27 would be at least in line with FY26. This has reduced the 'falling knife' risk and may signal an earnings floor. The business has been deliberately holding back sales to clear channel inventory in China and the US, meaning assets are under-earning. The whole business is trading below book value, making valuation attractive. Brand rationalisation toward premium labels like Penfolds is also increasingly being put into action.
quote: What happened in May? They had an investor day, and new CEO Sam Fisher gave earnings guidance for FY 26. That was slightly above market expectations. And also importantly, so that FY 27 would be at least in line with FY 26. The market has been incredibly fearful of catching the falling knife. We now potentially have some earnings stability and confidence that we are at the bottom now. That's really interesting because we know that Treasury have deliberately lowered their own earnings by holding back sales to get inventory out of the channel in China and in the US. And the assets are under earning. The whole business is trading below book value. Um, so perhaps this is the right time to kind of step in and have a look.
